title: feedback-driven-econ-autopilot-and-nudge-pipeline
author: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers tuning batching/caching/quantization defaults still need manual iterations when workload shifts. Motivation: Reduce engineering ops cycles and improve unit-econ stability by closing the loop: use live unit-economics signals (latency, tokens-per-request, error rate, model fallback frequency) to automatically propose safe nudges to batch size, cache TTLs, and quantization candidate tiers.

This PR introduces a feedback-driven econ autopilot pipeline that synthesizes per-tenant telemetry, runs a risk-aware optimizer, emits human-readable 'nudge' suggestions, and optionally surfaces safe automated rollouts for low-risk changes. Major goals: 1) produce high-signal, low-noise recommendations for batching and cache defaults; 2) add a transparent scoring and rollback mechanism; 3) make quantization profile suggestions conservative and traceable to evaluated regressions.

What changed (high level):
- New service: autosuggestor/econ-feedback-runner - ingests aggregated tenant telemetry and runs candidate scoring.
- New policy library: autosuggestor/policies/risk_thresholds.py - encapsulates allowed-change envelopes per SLA.
- Operator API: console endpoint /ops/tenants/{id}/econ-suggestions to view and apply suggestions with canary parameters.
- CLI dry-run: redwoodctl econ-sim --tenant <id> produces a simulated cost/latency delta and a recommended action set.
- Telemetry additions: new unit_econ signals (tokens_per_s, avg_tail_latency_95, fallback_count, cache_hit_ratio) and a compact snapshot proto for suggestion provenance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Synthetic offline sim harness and unit tests
- [x] End-to-end dry-run CLI
- [x] Console UI hook (backend only)
- [x] Safety gating via policy library
- [x] Telemetry tags and provenance metadata
- [x] Documentation draft in /docs/econ-autopilot.md (backend-focused)

Related: ENG-1429 (autopilot spec), ENG-1430 (telemetry contract). Also references earlier work: prefilling and quant presets (several PRs listed in repository history).

small_snippets:
--- autosuggestor/policies/risk_thresholds.py (excerpt)
ALLOWED_LATENCY_PCT_INCREASE = 0.08  # 8%
ALLOWED_TOKEN_COST_IMPROVEMENT = 0.03  # 3%
# conservative quant tier promotion only when regression < 0.5% on eval set

--- configs/defaults/econ_profiles.yaml (excerpt)
# per-tenant conservative defaults used as starting point
default_batch_size: 8
cold_cache_ttl_seconds: 30
quant_tier: safe (int8-dynamic)
review_comments: Rafael Torres (review): Nice end-to-end. A few questions: how do you avoid noisy signals from short spikes skewing recommendations? Can you sketch rate/aggregation windows?

Maya Chen (author): We use a combination of exponential smoothing for the per-tenant time series and a stability filter that requires a candidate delta to persist for three consecutive 10m windows (configurable). Details in autosuggestor/runner.py comments.
Anya Patel (review): The risk_thresholds file looks right but we need a way for SRE to override per-cluster policies. Add a cluster-level override hook in the policy API.
Maya Chen (author): Added cluster_override hook and a short integration test in test_risk_thresholds.py (verifies precedence).
Jonah Kim (review): CI failed on lint in first run — found a couple of unused imports and an async loop not awaited. Also pls ensure telemetry proto changes are backward compatible.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed lint and await issues, added versioned snapshot proto with optional fields and migration doc in docs/econ-autopilot.md. CI green now.

Includes a dry-run CLI and ops API for manual application and conservative automated rollouts behind risk thresholds.
